text: Fifteen years ago he had come to Kew with Lily. <break time="0.8s" /> And had begged her to marry him. <break time="0.8s" /> And as they sat by a lake. <break time="0.8s" /> A dragonfly kept circling round and round them. <break time="0.8s" /> In the heat. <break time="0.8s" /> How clearly he could still see the dragonfly. <break time="0.8s" /> And her shoe. <break time="0.8s" /> With the square silver buckle at the toe. <break time="0.8s" /> Moving impatiently while he spoke. <break time="0.8s" /> So that he knew her answer. <break time="0.8s" /> Without looking up at her face. <break time="0.8s" /> He had told himself. <break time="0.8s" /> That if the dragonfly settled on a leaf. <break time="0.8s" /> She would say Yes at once. <break time="0.8s" /> But it went round and round. <break time="0.8s" /> And never settled anywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And Lily had not married him. <break time="0.8s" /> Turning to his wife at last. <break time="0.8s" /> Simon asked her. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether she ever thought of the past. <break time="0.8s" /> And he confessed. <break time="0.8s" /> That he had been thinking of Lily. <break time="0.8s" /> The woman he might have married. <break time="0.8s" /> Far from minding. <break time="0.8s" /> Eleanor answered calmly. <break time="0.8s" /> That one always thought of the past. <break time="0.8s" /> In a garden. <break time="0.8s" /> Where men and women lay under the trees. <break time="0.8s" /> For they seemed to be the ghosts. <break time="0.8s" /> Of ones own happiness. <break time="0.8s" /> For her part. <break time="0.8s" /> She remembered six little girls. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting before their easels by a lake. <break time="0.8s" /> Twenty years ago. <break time="0.8s" /> Painting the first red water lilies she had ever seen. <break time="0.8s" /> When suddenly a kiss fell. <break time="0.8s" /> On the back of her neck. <break time="0.8s" /> It had been given. <break time="0.8s" /> She said. <break time="0.8s" /> By an old gray haired woman. <break time="0.8s" /> With a wart on her nose. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was the mother of all her kisses. <break time="0.8s" /> All her life. <break time="0.8s" /> Come, Caroline, come, Hubert, Eleanor called. <break time="0.8s" /> And the family walked on four abreast. <break time="0.8s" /> Until they diminished in size among the trees. <break time="0.8s" /> And looked half transparent. <break time="0.8s" /> In the trembling sunlight and shade.
